items.stem: What most justifies packaging a task as a reusable ChatGPT procedure?

options.text: The task recurs and benefits from consistent, repeatable output
options.rationale: Correct: reusability pays off for recurring tasks needing consistency.

options.text: The task will only ever be done once
options.rationale: A one-off task does not justify the overhead of packaging.

options.text: The procedure would use many adjectives
options.rationale: Wording style is not a reason to package a task.
Higher usage is not a benefit or a reason.

items.explanation: Correct: reusability pays off for recurring tasks needing consistency.

items.stem: Why version a shared procedure and keep a changelog?

options.text: So teams know what changed and can roll back if an update causes problems
options.rationale: Correct: versioning and a changelog make changes auditable and reversible.

options.text: Because versioning makes the model more accurate
options.rationale: Versioning does not affect model accuracy.

options.text: To hide the procedure from reviewers

options.rationale: Versioning is unrelated to context window size.

items.explanation: Correct: versioning and a changelog make changes auditable and reversible.

items.stem: Which TWO steps belong in change-control before a revised shared procedure goes live? (Select TWO)

options.text: Review and sign-off by an accountable owner
options.rationale: Correct: an accountable review gate is core to change-control.

options.text: Testing the revision for consistent output
options.rationale: Correct: testing confirms the change behaves as intended before rollout.
Deleting history removes the ability to roll back or audit.

items.explanation: Correct: an accountable review gate is core to change-control.
